answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a bonded identity registry: each agent locks a refundable deposit tied to one proven human, and only one active identity per human is allowed. Biometric attestation acts like a pigment, linking every wallet to a person, so a farm of ten thousand accounts must first recruit ten thousand verified humans. Registration also charges a non-refundable issuance fee, a steady pulse of cost. A duplicate found by clustering loses its whole bond and its human is blocked, setting in like marble. Sybil weight N thus needs N humans, N deposits and N fees, all at risk.
